input.prompt: The camera itself is completely locked off and motionless like a tripod photograph, with absolutely no zoom, no push-in, no drift, no pan and no camera movement of any kind for the entire clip. The framed 'NO JAPANESE SAKE, NO LIFE.' pop-art poster on the wall (a hand holding a wooden masu cup) stays perfectly rigid, flat and exactly the same size for the entire clip: its illustration, hand, masu cup, lettering, ALCOHOLIDAY logo, white border and proportions never warp, stretch, resize, shift position or change perspective, as if it truly is a static print and not a generated image. The only motion anywhere in this shot is the soft dappled sunlight and leaf shadows on the beige wall at the right side and on the wooden table: the shadows of tree leaves outside sway slowly and gently, as if a light breeze moves the branches, and the sunlight on the white tokkuri and sake cups shimmers softly. The leaf shadows stay on the wall beside the poster and on the table and never move the poster. Everything else, including the blurred tokkuri and sake cups in the foreground, the table, the wall and especially the framed poster, is completely still and motionless. A sunny, relaxed holiday afternoon in a Japanese tatami living room, warm natural sunlight, two old school friends enjoying chilled sake together. The sake is cold: no steam, no smoke, no haze. No faces are ever shown.
